reasons: Server data is written into the page without escaping, a security risk.
Relies on the browser's implicit event object in the tab switcher.

terms.meaning: a doorway other programs use to ask this app for data or actions, here the backend on port 8000.
the browser's built-in way to send a request to a server and wait for its answer.
the browser's live model of the page, which code reads and changes to update what the user sees.
a property that replaces the contents of a page area with HTML text, which can also run embedded script.
a plain text format for structured data made of named fields, used to talk to the backend.
checking something again on a fixed timer, here the backend status every 30 seconds.
values the program remembers while it runs, here currentData.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Backend address setting
sections.what: Stores the backend address that every request in this file uses, currently the local machine on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the address in one place so it is easy to change. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Changing the backend port here also requires changing the page links and the wizard file.

sections.name: currentData
sections.title: Shared memory of answers
sections.what: Holds the most recent answer from each tab so the download buttons can save them.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user download results later without asking the server again.
sections.watch_out: Data is lost on page reload because it is only kept in memory.

sections.name: document DOMContentLoaded handler
sections.title: Startup checks and timer
sections.what: When the page loads, it checks whether the backend is online and then repeats that check every 30 seconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the status badge up to date without a page refresh.
sections.watch_out: Each page keeps its own timer, so many open tabs send many status requests.

sections.name: showTab
sections.title: Switching between tabs
sections.what: Shows the chosen tab and hides the others, and loads the model list the first time the Browse Models tab opens.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page is a set of tabs in one page, so this switches between them.
sections.watch_out: It reads the global event object instead of receiving it as a parameter, which can break if the function is called in another way.

sections.name: checkAPIStatus
sections.title: Backend online status badge
sections.what: Asks the backend's documentation address whether it responds, then shows Online, Error, or Offline in the footer.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user a quick sign that the backend is reachable. Reason for using the documentation address is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Any successful response counts as online, so a backend that is up but broken can still show Online.

sections.name: showLoading
sections.title: Showing the loading overlay
sections.what: Displays the full-screen spinner that blocks clicks while a request runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops the user from sending repeated requests while waiting.
sections.watch_out: Every handler that calls it must also call the hide function, or the screen stays blocked.

sections.name: hideLoading
sections.title: Hiding the loading overlay
sections.what: Removes the full-screen spinner once a request finishes.
sections.why: Likely reason: pairs with the show function so the page is usable again.
sections.watch_out: It is called in the finally part of handlers, so it runs even after errors.

sections.name: showError
sections.title: Showing error messages
sections.what: Turns an error of any shape into readable text and places it in the chosen output area in red.
sections.why: Likely reason: the backend and the browser report errors in different shapes, so this converts them all into one message.
sections.watch_out: The message is inserted as raw HTML, so text containing markup from the server can change the page.

sections.name: handlePlanSurvey (part 1)
sections.title: Building the survey plan request
sections.what: Reads the planner form, sends the goal, audience, required topics and model type to the backend, then shows the planned questions as cards or raw data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the planner tab needs the backend to generate the plan, and this file turns the answer into readable cards.
sections.watch_out: Titles and question text from the backend are inserted without escaping.

sections.name: handlePlanSurvey (part 2)
sections.title: Showing planned questions
sections.what: Creates one card per planned question with its number, type, category and reasoning, then shows the result box.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes each planned question easy to scan. Reason for falling back to raw data is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the backend sends no survey_spec field, the page shows raw JSON instead of cards, which can hide a changed response format.

sections.name: handleAuthorQuestions (part 1)
sections.title: Sending the question author request
sections.what: Reads the topic, question type and count from the form, sends a request that describes them as one goal, then shows the generated questions.
sections.why: Likely reason: the author tab reuses the same backend endpoint style as the planner.
sections.watch_out: The audience is always sent as B2C and the count is only embedded in the goal text, so the backend cannot see them as separate settings.

sections.name: handleAuthorQuestions (part 2)
sections.title: Question author cleanup
sections.what: Shows an error in the author output area if the request fails and always hides the spinner afterwards.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the error display and spinner consistent with the other tabs.
sections.watch_out: The error path reuses the result box, so an old result may be replaced by an error message.

sections.name: handleValidate (part 1)
sections.title: Reading and checking the survey JSON
sections.what: Reads the pasted survey text, turns it into data, sends it to the validator endpoint, and starts showing the hard check results.
sections.why: Likely reason: the validator needs real data, so invalid text is rejected before any request is sent.
sections.watch_out: The audience is taken from the survey itself or defaults to B2C, which may not match the user's intent.

sections.name: handleValidate (part 2)
sections.title: Showing validation results
sections.what: Lists hard check problems, shows each quality score with colour, and lists suggestions.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates must-fix problems from optional quality advice.
sections.watch_out: A missing passed field is treated as a pass, so an incomplete answer may look healthy.

sections.name: loadModels
sections.title: Loading the model list
sections.what: Asks the backend for the model registry and stores the list so the page can display and filter it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list comes from the backend so it can change without editing the page.
sections.watch_out: Failure text is placed into the page as raw HTML.

sections.name: displayModels
sections.title: Drawing model cards
sections.what: Creates a card for each model showing its name, task, open source or paid label, provider, quality out of 10, and cost.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a readable overview of the models for choosing one.
sections.watch_out: Quality is multiplied by 10, so if the backend already sends a 0 to 10 score the number will be wrong.

sections.name: filterModels
sections.title: Filtering models by task and type
sections.what: Keeps only models matching the chosen task and access type, then redraws the cards.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user narrow a long list without another request.
sections.watch_out: If no list is loaded yet, it loads the list instead of filtering, which can surprise a user who only changed a dropdown.

sections.name: downloadJSON
sections.title: Saving stored answers as a file
sections.what: Turns the stored answer for a tab into a JSON file and starts a browser download with a timestamped name.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user keep results for their own records or debugging.
sections.watch_out: If nothing is stored yet, it shows an alert instead of a file.

sections.name: handleFileUpload (part 1)
sections.title: Uploading documents one at a time
sections.what: Reads the chosen files and document type, then sends each file separately to the upload endpoint, collecting successes and failures.
sections.why: Likely reason: one failing file should not stop the others. This is stated by the loop and error collection.
sections.watch_out: Files are sent in a loop, so a large batch takes a long time and the spinner stays up until all are done.

sections.name: handleFileUpload (part 2)
sections.title: Showing upload results and refreshing
sections.what: Lists which files uploaded with their IDs and which failed with reasons, resets the form, and reloads the document list.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives clear per-file feedback and clears the form for the next upload.
sections.watch_out: Failure reasons from the server are inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: loadDocuments
sections.title: Loading the document list
sections.what: Asks the backend for uploaded documents and stores them, then passes them to the display function.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the document list in sync after uploads.
sections.watch_out: Errors are written into the list area as raw HTML.

sections.name: displayDocuments
sections.title: Drawing document cards
sections.what: Creates a card for each uploaded document with its title, type, audience labels, ID, version and upload date.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user a quick view of what is in the knowledge base.
sections.watch_out: Only the first underscore in the document type is replaced, so types with several underscores display oddly. Titles are inserted as raw HTML.

summary: Browser logic for the classic single-page version of the research tool: it switches tabs and sends planner, author, validator, model list, and document upload requests to the backend.
purpose: Makes the buttons and forms on index.html work and shows the backend's answers on the page.
why: Likely reason: the page is plain HTML with no framework, so this file handles all the interaction. Reason for some specific choices is not stated in the code.
how: On page load it checks whether the backend is online and repeats that check every 30 seconds. Each tab has a handler that reads the form, sends a request to the backend, stores the answer in memory, and writes it into the page. Shared helpers show a spinner, show errors, and let the user download stored answers as files.
inputs: Form values typed by the user, files picked for upload, and JSON answers from the backend at the address stored in API_BASE_URL.
outputs: Updated text and cards on the page, a status badge showing whether the backend is online, downloaded JSON files, and in-memory data stored in currentData.
risks: Server text is inserted into the page as raw HTML, so a crafted response could run script in the browser. The author tab always sends the audience as B2C. The backend address is fixed to localhost.
debug: If a button does nothing, open the browser console and look for errors from the named function. If the status badge says Offline, confirm the backend is running on port 8000 and that the browser can reach it. If a result looks wrong, use the download button to see the raw answer.
